title: Seerah
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions about the life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: familiar people and places, the beginning of revelation, the Hijrah, and his caring everyday example. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory knowledge of the Prophet’s ﷺ life, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked hadith reports and biographical reference pages checked during preparation. Historical names and events are kept distinct from illustrative present-day scenarios. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: In which city was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born?
questions.explanation: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah.

references.label: Islamweb — The birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ father?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ father was Abdullah. Muhammad ibn Abdullah means Muhammad, son of Abdullah.

questions.question: What was the name of the Prophet's ﷺ mother?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ mother was Aminah, the daughter of Wahb.

references.label: Islamweb — Aminah, the mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: Which wife comforted the Prophet ﷺ after his first Quran revelation?
questions.explanation: Khadijah comforted him and spoke about his good character and care for others.

questions.question: In which cave did the Prophet ﷺ receive his first Quran verses?
questions.explanation: The first Quran verses came to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Hira.

questions.question: How old was the Prophet ﷺ when he began receiving revelation?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ began receiving revelation at the age of forty.

questions.question: To which city did the Prophet ﷺ migrate from Makkah in the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: The Hijrah was the Prophet's ﷺ migration from Makkah to Madinah.

questions.question: Which companion was with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave during the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ and was with him in the cave during the Hijrah.

questions.question: In which city did the Prophet ﷺ establish his mosque after the Hijrah?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ mosque is in Madinah. He established it after arriving there.

questions.question: Which of these women was a daughter of the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.explanation: Fatimah was one of the Prophet's ﷺ daughters. He welcomed her with love.

questions.question: How did the Prophet ﷺ show affection to the child Hasan in this report?
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ kissed Hasan and taught the importance of showing mercy.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do when passing a group of children?

options.text: Said greetings were only for adults

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ greeted children with salam. Children mattered to him too.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do at home?
questions.explanation: Aishah said the Prophet ﷺ helped his family at home and went to prayer when it was time.

questions.question: How did Anas describe the Prophet's ﷺ treatment of him?
questions.explanation: Anas served the Prophet ﷺ for years and remembered his gentle treatment.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ do if he did not want a food?

options.text: Mocked the person who made it
Called everyone foolish for eating it

questions.explanation: He ate food he liked and left what he did not want without finding fault with it.

questions.question: How was the Prophet ﷺ described when it came to giving?

options.text: Kind only when given a prize

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ was exceptionally generous, especially during Ramadan.

questions.question: How did Jarir remember the Prophet ﷺ receiving him?
questions.explanation: Jarir remembered the Prophet ﷺ welcoming him with a smile.

questions.question: Why did the Prophet ﷺ shorten a prayer after hearing a baby cry?

options.text: To avoid distressing the baby's mother

questions.explanation: He considered the mother's worry and kept the prayer shorter. His care included families with small children.

questions.question: What did people at Safa say about the Prophet's ﷺ truthfulness?

options.text: They knew him to invent stories
They knew him to tell the truth
They had never heard him speak

questions.explanation: Even people who opposed his message recognized his truthfulness when he addressed them at Safa.

questions.question: When given two choices, which would the Prophet ﷺ choose if it involved no sin?

options.text: The choice that made him boastful

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ chose ease when it did not involve sin. He did not choose a sinful action just to make things easier.

questions.question: What does calling Makkah the Prophet's ﷺ birthplace mean?

options.text: He first moved there after the Hijrah
It was the name of his father
It was the name of his mosque

questions.explanation: A birthplace is where someone is born. The Prophet ﷺ was born in Makkah.

references.label: Islamweb — The birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: What does Muhammad ibn Abdullah mean?
questions.explanation: In this name, ibn means son of. Abdullah was the Prophet's ﷺ father.

questions.question: Where does Aminah belong in a simple family chart of the Prophet ﷺ?
questions.explanation: Aminah was his mother. Remembering family names helps us learn his life story.

references.label: Islamweb — Aminah, the mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: What does Khadijah's response after the first revelation show?

options.text: She told him good character did not matter
She reassured him with caring words

questions.explanation: Khadijah listened and reassured him, remembering his truthfulness, family care and help for people in need.

questions.question: Which event is connected with the cave of Hira?

options.text: The first Quran verses came to the Prophet ﷺ
The Prophet's ﷺ mosque was built there
It became the city of Madinah
It was the Prophet's ﷺ birthplace

questions.explanation: Hira is connected with the beginning of Quran revelation. It is different from the cave used during the Hijrah.

questions.question: Was the Prophet ﷺ a child or an adult when he began receiving revelation?
questions.explanation: He was forty years old, already an adult, when revelation began.

questions.question: In the Prophet's ﷺ life story, what does the Hijrah to Madinah describe?

options.text: A journey from Madinah to Makkah for Hajj
A trip from Makkah to Taif
A move from Makkah to Madinah

questions.explanation: The Hijrah to Madinah was an important move in his life, from Makkah to Madinah.

questions.question: The Prophet ﷺ reassured Abu Bakr in the cave. Whose help did he remind him of?
questions.explanation: He reminded Abu Bakr of Allah's support. This teaches trust in Allah during difficulty.

questions.question: Which activity belonged in the mosque the Prophet ﷺ established in Madinah?
questions.explanation: The mosque was established for worship. The Prophet ﷺ and his companions prayed there.

questions.question: Fatimah was the Prophet's ﷺ daughter. What was he to her?
questions.explanation: A father and daughter are part of a family. The Prophet ﷺ was Fatimah's father.

questions.question: What does the Prophet's ﷺ affection toward Hasan teach?

options.text: Showing children loving care is good

questions.explanation: The report shows tenderness toward a child and teaches mercy. Loving care is part of good character.

questions.question: What can we learn from the Prophet ﷺ greeting children?

options.text: Salam is only for wealthy adults
Children must be ignored in public
Being younger removes a person's value
Children deserve a kind greeting too

questions.explanation: His greeting included children. We can follow this example by greeting others kindly.

questions.question: What does the Prophet's ﷺ help at home show?

options.text: Helping family is an honorable thing
Household help makes someone less important
Important people should refuse all help

questions.explanation: He helped his family. Caring behavior belongs at home as well as outside it.

questions.question: Which lesson fits Anas's memory of the Prophet ﷺ?

options.text: Treat helpers with patience and respect
Insults are the best way to teach
People who help must never be thanked

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ gentleness toward Anas gives us an example of patience with people who help us.

questions.question: Does leaving a food politely mean we must insult it first?

options.text: Yes, insults make leaving it polite
Yes, everyone must hear our complaint
No, we can leave it without insulting it
Yes, we must mock its cook

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ did not find fault with food. We can express preferences without hurtful comments.

questions.question: What does being generous mean?

options.text: Keeping every useful thing from others

questions.explanation: Generosity means being willing to give and help. The Prophet ﷺ was a great example of it.

questions.question: What does Jarir's memory of the Prophet's ﷺ smile show?

options.text: A warm way of welcoming someone
A way to make fun of someone
A demand that everyone hide sadness
A rule that people must never ask for help

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ smile was a friendly welcome. It did not teach us to mock people or hide every feeling.

questions.question: What does the shorter prayer for a crying baby's mother show?

options.text: He thought mothers' feelings did not matter
He wanted babies to be frightened

questions.explanation: He showed consideration for the mother's distress. His example teaches us to notice others' needs.

questions.question: Why is the people's answer at Safa important to his life story?

options.text: It proved honesty did not matter
It meant only friends could trust him
It showed that lying was admired

questions.explanation: Their answer shows his reputation for speaking truth. We can learn honesty from his example.

questions.question: Did the Prophet ﷺ choose something wrong just because it was easier?

options.text: Yes, ease made every wrong thing right
Yes, rules never mattered when something was easy
Yes, hurting others was allowed for convenience
No, the easier choice had to be free of sin

questions.explanation: He chose the easier option when it was not sinful. Ease does not make a wrong action right.

questions.question: Sara labels a map with the Prophet's ﷺ birthplace. Which city should she mark?
questions.explanation: Makkah is the city where Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.

references.label: Islamweb — The birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: Ayan's worksheet asks for the Prophet's ﷺ father's name. Which name should he write?
questions.explanation: His father's name was Abdullah. This is why he is called Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

questions.question: Maryam is matching the Prophet ﷺ with his mother. Which name should she choose?
questions.explanation: Aminah was the mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

references.label: Islamweb — Aminah, the mother of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

questions.question: After learning how Khadijah comforted the Prophet ﷺ, how could you support a worried friend?
questions.explanation: Khadijah's caring response gives us a lesson in reassurance. Listening kindly can help a worried friend.

questions.question: Your teacher asks which cave belongs with the beginning of Quran revelation. Which label should you choose?
questions.explanation: Choose Hira. The first Quran verses were revealed to the Prophet ﷺ there.

questions.question: You are making a life-story card for the start of revelation. Which age belongs on it?
questions.explanation: Revelation began when the Prophet ﷺ was forty years old.

questions.question: A learning game asks you to connect the two cities of the Prophet's ﷺ Hijrah. Which pair fits?
questions.explanation: The Hijrah route being learned here goes from Makkah to Madinah.

questions.question: Your class is matching companions with events. Who belongs beside the Prophet ﷺ in the Hijrah cave account?
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr was with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave during the Hijrah.

questions.question: Lina's lesson card says, "The Prophet's ﷺ Mosque." Which city should she match it with?
questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ Mosque is in Madinah, where he established it after the Hijrah.

questions.question: A family-tree activity needs one daughter of the Prophet ﷺ. Which name fits?
questions.explanation: Fatimah was one of the Prophet’s ﷺ daughters.

questions.question: You learn how tenderly the Prophet ﷺ treated Hasan. Which action follows that lesson with a younger child?

options.text: Mock the child for being small
Say children do not need care
Treat the child gently and kindly

questions.explanation: The Prophet's ﷺ affection toward Hasan teaches loving care for children. Gentleness is a way to practice this lesson.

questions.question: You pass some classmates after learning that the Prophet ﷺ greeted children. What can you do?

options.text: Say they are too young for greetings
Demand a gift before greeting them

questions.explanation: A kind salam follows the Prophet's ﷺ example of greeting children.

questions.question: You learn that the Prophet ﷺ helped at home. Which action follows his example?

options.text: Help your family put things away
Refuse because helping is beneath you
Make a mess for others to clear

questions.explanation: Helping with a suitable task at home follows his example of serving his family.

questions.question: A friend helping you drops some pencils. Remembering the Prophet's ﷺ gentleness with Anas, what should you do?

options.text: Speak kindly and help pick them up
Laugh until your friend feels ashamed

questions.explanation: Patient, respectful words follow the gentleness Anas remembered. We can help someone correct a mistake without insulting them.

questions.question: You are offered food you do not like. Which response follows the Prophet's ﷺ manners?

options.text: Politely decline without insulting the food
Tell everyone they are foolish for liking it

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ left unwanted food without criticizing it. You can be polite about your preferences too.

questions.question: After learning about the Prophet's ﷺ generosity, which action can you practice?

options.text: Take someone else's toy to give away
Share something suitable that you have permission to give

questions.explanation: Sharing what you may give is one way to practice generosity. The Prophet ﷺ showed great generosity.

questions.question: A new classmate arrives. Which welcome reflects the Prophet's ﷺ warm treatment of Jarir?

options.text: Offer a friendly smile and welcome
Make fun of the classmate's name
Ignore them to show you are important

questions.explanation: A friendly welcome can help someone feel included. Jarir remembered being received warmly by the Prophet ﷺ.

questions.question: After learning about the crying baby, you notice a parent needs help carrying a bag. Which response shows consideration?

options.text: Offer suitable help with an adult nearby
Say other people's needs never matter

questions.explanation: His care for a worried mother teaches consideration. Offering suitable help is an everyday example of noticing someone's needs.

questions.question: You learn that people recognized the Prophet's ﷺ honesty. You accidentally break a pencil. What follows his example?

options.text: Blame someone who was not there
Invent a story to avoid responsibility
Tell the truth about what happened

questions.explanation: Speaking truthfully follows his example. Be honest about what happened and ask how to put things right.

questions.question: Two allowed ways finish a task well. One is simpler. Which choice fits the Prophet's ﷺ example?

options.text: Make the task harder just to boast
Use the simpler way without doing wrong

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ chose the easier option when it was not sinful. A simple, honest way can be a good choice.
